intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome (ABERS) is caused by mutation in the TBX22 gene (300307) on chromosome Xq21.1.

checks.explanation: Chromosomal location is standard nomenclature. The abstract establishes that TBX22 is X-linked.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome is a syndrome characterized by cleft palate, coloboma, hypospadias, deafness, short stature, and radial synostosis (Abruzzo and Erickson, 1977). The deafness is sensorineural (Pauws et al., 2013). Although the disorder has been described as CHARGE-like, Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) concluded that their patients did not have familial CHARGE syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) did a follow-up study of the family they had reported in 1977. This family had been cited as an example of familial CHARGE syndrome, but after re-evaluation the authors concluded that the patients did not have familial CHARGE syndrome. They referred to the disorder as a new X-linked syndrome.

paragraphs.text: Abruzzo and Erickson (1977) concluded that the family history suggested either autosomal dominant inheritance with limited expression in females or X-linked inheritance. Abruzzo and Erickson (1989) later referred to the disorder as X-linked. Pauws et al. (2013) identified a mutation in the X-linked TBX22 gene that tracked with the phenotype in the family, consistent with X-linked inheritance.

paragraphs.text: Hypothesizing a possible involvement of TBX22 in the X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome family of unknown etiology originally reported by Abruzzo and Erickson (1977), Pauws et al. (2013) identified a novel splice acceptor mutation in the TBX22 gene (c.593-5T-A) that tracked with the phenotype in the family. In patients with classic X-linked cleft palate phenotypes, they found a novel TBX22 splice donor variant (c.767+5G-A) and a known canonical splice donor mutation (c.767+1G-A), affecting the same exon as the Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome mutation. In silico and in vitro splicing studies predicted that all 3 variants abolished normal mRNA splicing, and an in vitro assay indicated that use of alternative splice sites was a likely outcome. Pauws et al. (2013) concluded that TBX22 is the gene underlying Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, expanding the phenotypic spectrum of TBX22 mutations.

clinical_synopsis.feature: coloboma of the optic nerve head

paragraphs.text: In affected members of the family with X-linked, CHARGE-like Abruzzo-Erickson syndrome, featuring sensorineural deafness and coloboma, Pauws et al. (2013) identified a novel c.593-5T-A splice acceptor mutation in the TBX22 gene. The mutation tracked with the phenotype in the family. In silico and in vitro splicing studies predicted that the variant abolished normal mRNA splicing, and an in vitro assay indicated that use of alternative splice sites was a likely outcome.
